name: Jenny Lake Ranger Station
summary: Exterior-only reconstruction of the relocated Lee Mangus/Manges homestead cabin using HABS WY-108 for geometry and the exact named Jenny Lake Ranger Station footprint for runtime placement.

included: Lee Mangus/Manges cabin fabric and documented 1937 east-end addition
attached entrance porch and exterior steps
immediate ground contact needed to seat the cabin beneath the existing tree canopy
excluded: Jenny Lake Visitor Center and its Crandall Studio fabric
James or Jimmy Manges Cabin near Cottonwood Creek
other Jenny Lake Ranger Station Historic District buildings
visitor-service props, people, permit displays, and temporary signs

structures.name: Jenny Lake Ranger Station (Lee Mangus/Manges Cabin)

placement.strategy: Select the exact named Jenny Lake Ranger Station record, retain its polygon without buffering or rectangular replacement, and use HABS WY-108 to reconcile the wall envelope, porch, height, and orientation. Re-resolve by exact name and compare the source-file hash before every deterministic rebuild.

features.source_height_policy: Do not use as measured architectural truth; HABS WY-108 documents an 18-foot ridge height. Treat the extract height as a placement-dataset value to be reconciled before export.

known_excluded_footprints.name: Jenny Lake Visitor Center
known_excluded_footprints.reason: The relocated Harrison Crandall Studio is a different building and is outside this candidate.

known_excluded_footprints.name: Manges Cabin
known_excluded_footprints.reason: This repository record is the separate James/Jimmy Manges Cabin near Cottonwood Creek, not Lee Manges' relocated cabin.

resolution_steps: Hash terrain/public/buildings.json and persist the hash in the run artifact.
Resolve exactly one record named Jenny Lake Ranger Station; reject zero or multiple matches.
Reject any selector or fallback that resolves Jenny Lake Visitor Center or Manges Cabin.
Compare the resolved vertices, centroid, and source height with this package snapshot.
Fit the HABS 20-foot-6-inch by 36-foot-9-inch wall envelope and documented porch within the named current footprint; quarantine rather than scale non-uniformly if they cannot be reconciled.
Use the current terrain sampler for ground elevation and re-basing; never bake an assumed absolute elevation.
Confirm the west entrance and building axis against the HABS north arrow and current same-building evidence before capture approval.

budgets.material_policy: Use one compact weathered-log and wood-shingle atlas with a small registered entrance treatment only if source-image rights clear. Keep glazing, stone, and dark hardware within the primitive budget.

lods.intent: Retain measured openings, saddle-notched log ends, entrance porch, gable truss, restrained stone footing, and close canopy contact.
Retain the long gabled cabin, west entrance porch, primary door and window rhythm, and documented east-end addition.
Preserve the low rectangular wall mass, steep gable silhouette, and west porch projection.

required_views.purpose: Entrance porch, vertical-plank door, multi-light window, diagonal-log king-post gable treatment, and public identity.
Long-wall proportions, three-window rhythm, log courses, addition junction, and roof character.
Documented east-end addition, door and window positions, and gable-end log treatment.

prompt_constraints: Preserve the exact registered target silhouette, measured roof, porch, openings, crop, camera, and transparent/background mask.
Use only references proven to depict the Jenny Lake Ranger Station built from Lee Mangus/Manges' cabin.
Exclude the Crandall Studio Jenny Lake Visitor Center and the separate James/Jimmy Manges Cabin near Cottonwood Creek.
Keep HABS-documented saddle-jointed horizontal log walls, wood-shingle gable roof, stone footing, multi-light windows, plank doors, west entrance porch, and diagonal-log gable treatment.
Do not infer geometry, dimensions, placement, roof topology, openings, additions, or interior content from image generation.
Do not add people, visitor displays, modern furniture, vehicles, text, watermark, landscape, lake, mountains, sky, featureless black rectangles, or baked directional shadows.
Keep tileable materials free of perspective, vegetation, sky, and directional sunlight.

checks: single-candidate triangle, material-primitive, and texture budgets
one active LOD for the landmark
HABS envelope, ridge height, porch, and opening registration
projection registration at frontal and grazing angles
closed exterior envelope with no walkable interior
existing canopy, paths, and visitor-area context retained outside physical clearance
no production asset or manifest mutation
